sanskrit: ūrdhvā asya samidho bhavanty ūrdhvā śukrā śocīṃṣy agneḥ | dyumattamā supratīkasya sūnos tanūnapād asuro viśvavedāḥ ||
english: Upward rise his kindling-sticks, upward blaze the bright flames of Agni; most resplendent is the son of the fair-visaged one — Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the All-knowing.

sanskrit: devo deveṣu devaḥ patho anakti madhvā ghṛtena | madhvā yajñaṃ nakṣati prīṇāno narāśaṃsaḥ sukṛd devaḥ savitā viśvavāraḥ ||
english: The god among gods, the god who anoints the paths with honey and ghee — gladly he attends the sacrifice with sweetness: Narāśaṃsa, the beneficent god Savitā, the All-desirable.

sanskrit: acchāyam eti śavasā ghṛtena- -īḍe vahniṃ namasāgnim | sruco adhvareṣu prayatsu ||
english: He goes forth unimpeded, with might and with ghee — I praise the bearer, I reverence Agni; the sacrificial ladles are proffered at the rites.

sanskrit: sa yakṣad asya mahimānam agneḥ sa in mandrāsu prayatsu | vasoś cetiṣṭho vasudhātamaś ca ||
english: He shall worship the greatness of this Agni, even he, amid the gladsome oblations duly offered; most discerning is he of Vasu, and the greatest dispenser of wealth.

sanskrit: dvāro devīr annasya viśve vratā dadante agneḥ | uruvyacaso dhāmnā patyamānāḥ ||
english: The divine doors of food, all vows of Agni, bestow their gifts — they, of broad compass, ruling by their own domain.

sanskrit: te asya vṛṣaṇo divyā nu yonā | uṣāsānaktemaṃ yajñam avatām adhvaraṃ naḥ ||
english: These are his divine bull-like sources; may Night-and-Dawn, the two, protect this sacrifice, our faultless rite.

sanskrit: daivā hotāra imam adhvaraṃ no agner jihvem abhi gṛṇīta | kṛṇutā naḥ sviṣṭim ||
english: O divine Hotṛ-priests, with the tongue of Agni praise this our faultless rite; make for us a well-performed oblation.

sanskrit: tisro devīr barhir edaṃ sadantv iḍā sarasvatī mahī | bhāratī gṛṇānā ||
english: Let the three goddesses take their seat upon this sacred grass — Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī — with Bhāratī singing praise.

sanskrit: tan nas turīpam adbhutaṃ purukṣu | tvaṣṭā suvīryaṃ rāyaspoṣaṃ vi syarta nābhim asme ||
english: That wondrous, sustaining power, abounding in nourishment — may Tvaṣṭṛ loosen the hub of heroic strength and opulence of riches for us.

sanskrit: vanaspate ava sṛjā rarāṇas tmanā devebhyaḥ | agnir havyaṃ śamitā sūdayāti ||
english: O Lord of the Forest, release freely of thyself to the gods; Agni, the Immolator, sets the oblation rightly in order.

sanskrit: agne svāhā kṛṇu jātaveda indrāya bhāgam | viśve devā havir idaṃ juṣantām ||
english: O Agni, Jātavedas, make svāhā — assign the portion to Indra; may all the gods take pleasure in this oblation.

sanskrit: yajūṃṣi yajñe samidhaḥ svāhā- -agniḥ pravidvān iha vo yunaktu | yunaktu devaḥ savitā prajānann asmin yajñe suyujaḥ svāhā ||
english: Yajus-formulas in the sacrifice, the kindling-sticks — svāhā! May Agni, the all-knowing, yoke you here; may god Savitā, the all-discerning, yoke you well in this sacrifice — svāhā!

sanskrit: indra ukthāmadāni yajñe asmin pravidvān yunaktu suyujaḥ svāhā | chandāṃsi yajñaṃ marutaḥ svāhā māteva putraṃ pipṛteha yuktāḥ ||
english: May Indra, gladdened by the recitations, all-knowing, yoke aright in this sacrifice — svāhā! May the Maruts, with the metres, nourish the sacrifice here — svāhā — even as a mother nourishes her son, themselves well-yoked.

sanskrit: praiṣā nivida āpriyo yajūṃṣi śiṣṭāḥ patnībhir vahateha yuktāḥ | eyam agan barhiṣā prokṣaṇībhir yajñaṃ tanvānā aditiḥ svāhā ||
english: The invitatory calls, the niviḍ-formulas, the āprī-verses, the Yajus-texts — hither they have come, yoked, borne by the wives; Aditi has come hither with the sacred grass and the sprinkling-waters, extending the sacrifice — svāhā!

sanskrit: viṣṇur yunaktu bahudhā tapāṃsy asmin yajñe suyujaḥ svāhā ||
english: May Viṣṇu yoke in manifold ways the fervent energies in this sacrifice, well-yoked — svāhā!

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā yunaktu bahudhā nu rūpāṇy asmin yajñe (…) ||
english: May Tvaṣṭṛ yoke in manifold ways the forms in this sacrifice [— well-yoked — svāhā!]

sanskrit: indro yunaktu bahudhā vīryāny asmin (…) ||
english: May Indra yoke in manifold ways the heroic powers in this [sacrifice — well-yoked — svāhā!]

sanskrit: somo yunaktu bahudhā payāṃsy asmin (…) ||
english: May Soma yoke in manifold ways the milk-streams in this [sacrifice — well-yoked — svāhā!]

sanskrit: bhago yunaktv āśiṣo nv asmā asmin yajñe suyujaḥ svāhā ||
english: May Bhaga yoke forthwith the blessings for us in this sacrifice, well-yoked — svāhā!

sanskrit: aśvinā brahmaṇetam arvāg vaṣaṭkāreṇa yajñaṃ vardhayantau svāhā ||
english: O Aśvinau, come hither with the Brahman-prayer, augmenting the sacrifice with the vaṣaṭ-call — svāhā!

sanskrit: bṛhaspate brahmaṇehy arvāṅ yajño 'yaṃ svar idaṃ yajamānāya dhehi svāhā ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, come hither with the Brahman-prayer; this sacrifice is thine — bestow this heavenly light upon the sacrificer — svāhā!

sanskrit: āpaḥ punantu varuṇaḥ punātv ayaṃ ca yaḥ pavate viśvadānīm | yajño bhago adhivaktā vidhartā- -agniś ca naḥ pāvayetāṃ sūryaś ca ||
english: May the Waters purify; may Varuṇa purify; and may he who flows, ever bestowing all things, purify — may Yajña, Bhaga, the Advocate, the Dispenser, and Agni, and Sūrya, all purify us.

sanskrit: daśaśīrṣo daśajihva ā rabhe vīrako bhiṣak | mā te riṣaṃ khanitā yasmai ca tvā khanāmasi ||
english: I, Vīraka the healer, ten-headed and ten-tongued, take hold of thee; may no harm come to the digger or to him for whose sake we dig thee.

sanskrit: daśarātre kilāsasya vīrudhā veda bheṣajam | itas tad abhriyākhanaṃ kilāsaṃ nāśayāmi te ||
english: In ten nights the plant knows the remedy for kilāsa; digging it from here as one digs from a cloud, I destroy the kilāsa for thee.

sanskrit: apsv anyā vi rohati dhanvany anyādhi tiṣṭhati | kilāsam anyānīnaśad varcasānyā sam ukṣatu ||
english: One variety grows in the waters, another stands upon the arid land; let another annihilate the kilāsa, let another sprinkle it away with radiance.

sanskrit: ājyena ghṛtena juhomi kilāsabheṣajam | vīrudhām agneḥ saṅkāśe kilāsaṃ nānu vidyate ||
english: With ājya, with ghee, I offer oblation as the remedy for kilāsa; in the presence of the plants, before Agni, kilāsa is found no more.

sanskrit: piśaṅgarūpo bhavati kalmāṣam uta saṃdṛśi | kilāsa naśyetaḥ paraḥ pra tvā dhakṣyāmi vīrudhā ||
english: It becomes tawny-hued, and spotted too in appearance; O kilāsa, perish hence, away! I shall burn thee up with the plant.

sanskrit: yāni pṛthag utpatanti nakṣatrāṇīva saṃdṛśi | kilāsaṃ sarvaṃ nāśayann ogha ivābhy emi vīrudhā ||
english: Those spots that break out separately, like stars in appearance — I approach with the plant to destroy all kilāsa, like a flood.

sanskrit: yadi vā puruṣeṣitāt kilāsa paryājagan | namo namasyāmo devān pratyak kartāram ṛcchatu ||
english: If, O kilāsa, thou hast come from being caused by a man's will, we bow, we pay reverence; may it turn back upon the very perpetrator.

sanskrit: śīrṣṇas te skandhebhyo lalāṭāt pari karṇayoḥ | oṣadhyā varṣajūtayā kilāsaṃ nāśayāmi te | svas tvā varṇa āyaty anarātiḥ sahauṣadhiḥ ||
english: From thy head, thy shoulders, thy brow, round about thy ears — with the rain-impelled herb I destroy the kilāsa for thee; thine own colour comes to thee tomorrow, free from affliction, together with the plant.

sanskrit: grīvābhyas ta uṣṇihābhyaḥ kīkasābhyo anūkyāt | (…) ||
english: From thy neck, thy nape, thy vertebrae, from thy spine — [with the rain-impelled herb I destroy the kilāsa for thee; thine own colour comes to thee tomorrow, free from affliction, together with the plant.]

sanskrit: aṃsābhyāṃ te dorbhyāṃ bāhubhyāṃ pari hastayoḥ | (…) ||
english: From thy shoulders, thy forearms, thy upper arms, round about thy hands — [with the rain-impelled herb I destroy the kilāsa for thee; thine own colour comes to thee tomorrow, free from affliction, together with the plant.]

sanskrit: pṛṣṭibhyas te pārśvābhyāṃ śroṇibhyāṃ pari bhaṃsasaḥ | (…) ||
english: From thy back, thy flanks, thy hips, round about thy buttocks — [with the rain-impelled herb I destroy the kilāsa for thee; thine own colour comes to thee tomorrow, free from affliction, together with the plant.]

sanskrit: ūrubhyāṃ te 'ṣṭhīvadbhyāṃ pārṣṇibhyāṃ prapadābhyām | oṣadhyā varṣajūtayā kilāsaṃ nāśayāmi te | svas tvā varṇa āyaty anarātiḥ sahauṣadhiḥ ||
english: From thy thighs, thy knees, thy heels, thy forefeet — with the rain-impelled herb I destroy the kilāsa for thee; thine own colour comes to thee tomorrow, free from affliction, together with the plant.
